definitions.definition: Anything that possesses mass and occupies physical space (volume).
The shiny or glossy appearance of a freshly cut or polished metal surface.
Materials that allow light to pass through completely, making objects behind clearly visible.
Materials that allow light to pass through partially, making objects behind appear blurred.
Materials that do not allow light to pass through at all.
A quantitative measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
A glass thermometer with a capillary kink designed to measure human body temperature between 35°C and 42°C.
A thermometer used in scientific experiments to measure temperatures from -10°C to 110°C.
The process by which liquid water changes into water vapor at temperatures below its boiling point.

definitions.definition: The method of separating lighter husk particles from heavier food grains using blowing wind currents.
The settling down of heavy insoluble solid particles at the bottom of a liquid mixture when left undisturbed.
The process of gently pouring off the upper clear liquid without disturbing the settled sediment.
The process of passing a liquid mixture containing insoluble solids through a porous filter to separate residue from filtrate.
The cellular process by which living organisms break down food to release energy.
The biological process of eliminating toxic metabolic waste products from an organism's body.
The process by which a dormant seed sprouts and begins growing into a seedling when supplied with water, air, and warmth.
The dark organic topsoil layer formed by soil micro-organisms decomposing fallen dry leaves and organic litter.
A recognizable pattern formed by a group of stars in the night sky named after figures or animals.
A star fixed above Earth's geographic North Pole used for celestial compass navigation.

concepts.description: Science is an interconnected body of knowledge where every new discovery acts as a puzzle piece completing our understanding of nature.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science

concepts.description: Plants are categorized into herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers, and creepers based on height, stem hardness, and branching location.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 2: Diversity in the Living World

concepts.description: Organisms possess specific physical adaptations (e.g. webbed feet in ducks, needle leaves in mountain trees, spines in cacti) tailored to their habitat.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 2: Diversity in the Living World

concepts.description: A healthy diet combines carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, roughage, and water in appropriate proportions.
Native Indian millets (Jowar, Bajra, Ragi, Sanwa) provide high nutrient density while requiring minimal irrigation.
Magnetic attraction is strongest at the North and South poles and weakest at the center of a bar magnet.
A freely suspended magnet always aligns itself along Earth's geographic North-South direction.
Informal body measurements (handspan, cubit) vary between individuals, requiring standard SI units like the meter for consistency.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion

concepts.description: Objects exhibit rectilinear motion (straight line), circular motion (curved orbit around central point), or periodic motion (regular repeating intervals).
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion

concepts.concept_name: Classification of Matter by Physical Properties
concepts.description: Materials are grouped based on lustre, hardness, solubility, density/floating, and transparency.

concepts.concept_name: Limitations of Human Touch for Temperature
concepts.description: Human touch sensation is relative and deceptive, necessitating calibrated thermometers for objective temperature measurement.
Water transitions continuously between solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapor) through heating and cooling.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

concepts.description: Solar evaporation and transpiration lift water vapor into the atmosphere, where cooling forms clouds that return rain to Earth.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

concepts.description: Mixtures are separated exploiting physical differences such as particle size (sieving), weight (winnowing), gravity (sedimentation), solubility (evaporation), or magnetism.
All living entities share nutrition, growth, respiration, response to stimuli, excretion, reproduction, and finite lifespans.
Dry seeds maintain minimal metabolic rate (dormancy) and resume active germination when provided with water, air, and warmth.

concepts.concept_name: Forest Ecosystem Services and Soil Binding
concepts.description: Forests generate oxygen, decompose leaf litter into humus, and bind topsoil with root networks to prevent erosion.
The Sun is orbited by eight planets; constellations in dark, unpolluted night skies enable celestial navigation.

principles_laws.statement: Scientific inquiry follows systematic stages: Observation -> Questioning -> Hypothesis -> Experimentation -> Analysis and Conclusion.
principles_laws.source_reference: Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science

principles_laws.statement: Like magnetic poles repel each other (N-N, S-S repel), whereas opposite magnetic poles attract each other (N-S attracts).
Repulsion is the only conclusive test for confirming that an object is a magnet, because attraction occurs with unmagnetized iron as well.
Magnetic poles always exist in inseparable pairs; breaking a magnet creates two smaller complete magnets, each with North and South poles.
To prevent parallax measurement error, the observer's eye must be positioned vertically directly above the scale mark being read.
principles_laws.source_reference: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion

principles_laws.statement: All physical matter universally possesses mass and occupies physical space (volume).
Hitabhuk, Ritabhuk, Mitabhuk: Eat wholesome food, eat seasonal food, and eat in measured moderation.
The rate of liquid evaporation is directly proportional to the exposed liquid surface area.
principles_laws.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

principles_laws.statement: Insoluble solid particles denser than the liquid medium settle to the bottom under gravitational force when left undisturbed.
A dense atmosphere dominated by carbon dioxide traps solar thermal radiation, creating extreme surface temperatures.

processes.description: Inflate tube, submerge in water bowl, observe escaping air bubbles rising to pinpoint pinhole leak.
processes.source_reference: Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science

processes.description: Stroke an unmagnetized iron piece repeatedly (30-40 times) in one direction along its length using one fixed pole of a bar magnet.
Lay a flexible thread along a curved contour, mark start and end points with knots, and stretch taut along a flat meter ruler.
processes.source_reference: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion

processes.description: Add teaspoon of solid sample into glass of water, stir vigorously for 1 minute, allow to stand, and observe if particles dissolve or settle.
Wash thermometer, shake down mercury below 35°C, place bulb under tongue for 1 minute, remove horizontally at eye level, and read scale.
Solar radiation evaporates surface water -> warm vapor rises -> cools in upper atmosphere -> condenses into microscopic water droplets around dust particles -> forms floating clouds.
processes.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

processes.process_name: Harvesting Common Salt from Sea Water
processes.description: Trap sea water in shallow coastal pans -> allow solar radiation to evaporate liquid -> collect and refine solid crude salt crystals.
Fold paper circle into cone -> insert into glass funnel -> pour muddy mixture -> collect clear filtrate liquid below while mud remains as residue on paper.
Hydrate dry seeds with moisture -> absorb oxygen for cellular respiration -> keep in warm environment -> seed coat splits -> radicle (root) and plumule (shoot) emerge.
Dry leaves fall onto forest floor -> soil micro-organisms decompose organic plant litter over time -> dark nutrient-rich topsoil layer forms.
Locate Saptarishi bowl -> identify two outer pointer stars -> extend imaginary straight line through them -> line points directly to Dhruva Tara (Pole Star).

structures_functions.structure: Fleshy Stems and Spines of Desert Cacti
structures_functions.function: Spines (modified leaves) reduce transpiration water loss; thick green stems store water and perform photosynthesis.
structures_functions.source_reference: Chapter 2: Diversity in the Living World

structures_functions.function: Prevents mercury column from falling back into the bulb automatically when removed from patient's mouth.
Physically entwine and bind soil particles together, preventing rainwater streams from causing soil erosion.
Traditional stepped stone structures engineered to capture rainwater, shade storage from evaporation, and recharge aquifers.
structures_functions.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

structures_functions.function: Electronic device that extracts ambient humidity from air and cools it to condense clean drinking water.
structures_functions.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

structures_functions.function: Pivoted magnetized iron needle that rotates freely to indicate Earth's North-South magnetic meridian.
Microscopic porous paper barrier that permits liquid filtrate to pass while trapping insoluble solid residue.

cause_effect.cause: Air pressure leak in punctured inner tube submerged in water
cause_effect.effect: Visible air bubbles rise through water surface revealing puncture location.
cause_effect.source_reference: Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science

cause_effect.cause: Heating, hammering, or dropping a bar magnet onto hard ground
cause_effect.effect: Destruction of internal domain alignment causing complete demagnetization.

cause_effect.cause: Viewing a scale mark at an inclined angle instead of vertically
cause_effect.effect: Apparent displacement error known as Parallax Error.
cause_effect.source_reference: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion

cause_effect.cause: Increasing exposed surface area of liquid water (e.g. wide plate vs bottle cap)
cause_effect.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

cause_effect.cause: Contact of warm atmospheric water vapor with ice-cold glass tumbler wall
cause_effect.effect: Cooling of gas below dew point causing condensation into liquid droplets on outer wall.
cause_effect.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

cause_effect.cause: Physical contact with leaflets of Mimosa pudica (Chhui-mui)
cause_effect.effect: Rapid folding inward of leaflets and drooping of leaf stalk.

cause_effect.cause: Clear-cutting forests and removing tree cover on hillslopes
cause_effect.effect: Loss of soil root binding leading to severe topsoil erosion and mudslides.

cause_effect.cause: Burning fallen dry leaves on ground
cause_effect.effect: Air pollution, CO2 release, destruction of organic material for humus, and death of soil micro-organisms.

cause_effect.cause: Thick dense atmosphere dominated by carbon dioxide on Venus
cause_effect.effect: Extreme runaway greenhouse effect making Venus hotter than Mercury.

cause_effect.cause: Excessive artificial street lighting in cities
cause_effect.effect: Light pollution that obscures visibility of dim celestial stars.

relationships.relationship_name: Distance from Sun vs Planetary Sequence
relationships.mathematical_or_logical_correlation: Mercury (1) -> Venus (2) -> Earth (3) -> Mars (4) -> Jupiter (5) -> Saturn (6) -> Uranus (7) -> Neptune (8).

relationships.relationship_name: Saptarishi Pointer Stars to Pole Star
relationships.mathematical_or_logical_correlation: Extending a straight line through the two outer bowl stars of Saptarishi intersects Dhruva Tara (Pole Star).

observations.details: When an inflated punctured tube is held underwater, a stream of air bubbles escapes continuously from the pinhole.
observations.source_reference: Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science

observations.details: When rolled in steel paperclips, maximum clips cling to the two ends (poles) and almost none stick at the center.
A freely suspended bar magnet rotates and comes to rest pointing strictly along Earth's North-South meridian.
Measuring the same classroom table with handspans of different students yields different numerical counts.
observations.source_reference: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion

observations.observation_title: Salt vs Sand Solubility in Water
observations.details: Salt stirs into water forming a clear solution; sand settles undisturbed at the bottom of the tumbler.
Lukewarm water feels warm to a hand previously dipped in cold water, but cold to a hand dipped in hot water.

observations.observation_title: Bottle Cap vs Wide Plate Evaporation Comparison
observations.details: Equal water volumes left in sunlight evaporate completely from a wide plate hours before the bottle cap dries.
observations.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

observations.details: Warm water in a jar covered by an ice tray creates visible mist/fog floating inside the jar.
observations.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

observations.details: Touching a leaflet of Mimosa pudica causes adjacent leaflets to fold together within seconds.
Dry bean seeds kept on moist cotton in warmth swell, split their coats, and sprout white radicles within 48 hours.

experiments_activities.procedure: Submerge inflated bicycle inner tube in water bowl, locate escaping air bubbles, mark puncture.
experiments_activities.source_reference: Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 2.1: School Nature Walk Biodiversity Survey
experiments_activities.procedure: Walk through garden, record plant stem hardness, leaf venation, bird calls, and animal locomotion.
experiments_activities.source_reference: Chapter 2: Diversity in the Living World

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 3.1: Nutrition Label Analysis (Wafers vs Chana)
experiments_activities.procedure: Compare nutritional information on potato wafer packet vs roasted chana packet for fat, sodium, protein, and fiber content.

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 4.1: Magnetic Testing of Classroom Items
experiments_activities.procedure: Touch bar magnet to paperclip, pencil, eraser, key, copper strip; classify items as magnetic or non-magnetic.

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 4.2: Single-Touch Magnetization of Sewing Needle
experiments_activities.procedure: Stroke steel needle 30-40 times with one pole of bar magnet in one direction; float on cork in water to test compass action.

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 5.1: Measuring Table Length with Handspans vs Ruler
experiments_activities.procedure: Record table width using student handspans, compare variance, then measure with standard meter scale.
experiments_activities.source_reference: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 5.2: Measuring Perimeter of Curved Leaf using Thread
experiments_activities.procedure: Align flexible thread along leaf contour, knot start/end points, stretch thread taut on ruler to read length.
experiments_activities.source_reference: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 6.1: Material Solubility Testing in Water Tumblers
experiments_activities.procedure: Add salt, sugar, chalk powder, sand, and sawdust into water tumblers; stir and observe solubility after 1 minute.
Dip left hand in cold water A, right hand in hot water C for 1 minute; transfer both to lukewarm water B and record sensations.

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 8.1: Evaporation Rate Comparison (Bottle Cap vs Wide Plate)
experiments_activities.procedure: Pour equal 10 mL water into narrow cap and wide plate, leave in sun, measure time required for complete dryness.
experiments_activities.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 9.1: Muddy Water Filtration using Filter Paper Cone
experiments_activities.procedure: Fold filter paper cone, insert into funnel, pour muddy water, collect clear filtrate in beaker.

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 10.1: Seed Germination in Moist Cotton
experiments_activities.procedure: Place dry bean seeds on wet cotton wool in dish, maintain moisture and warmth, observe daily root/shoot growth.

experiments_activities.activity_name: Activity 12.1: Locating Dhruva Tara via Saptarishi
experiments_activities.procedure: Observe northern night sky, find Saptarishi constellation, locate bowl pointer stars, extend line to find fixed Pole Star.

applications.description: Submerging inner tubes in water identifies pinhole air leaks so rubber patches can be applied.
applications.source_reference: Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science

applications.description: Utilizes Earth's magnetic field alignment for direction finding across ocean traversals and desert travel.
Large electromagnets extract magnetic iron scrap from municipal solid waste streams.

applications.application_title: Standardized SI Measurement in Construction and Trade
applications.description: Using global standard SI meter scales ensures architectural precision and fair trade transactions.
applications.source_reference: Chapter 5: Measurement of Length and Motion

applications.application_title: Selection of Insulating Handles on Metallic Cookware
applications.description: Crafting pan bodies from thermal conductors (aluminum/copper) and handles from insulators (plastic/wood) prevents burn injuries.
Clinical thermometers allow accurate detection of human fever (temperatures above 37.0°C).

applications.application_title: Harvesting Common Salt in Coastal Evaporation Pans
applications.description: Trapping ocean water in shallow pans allows solar radiation to evaporate liquid, producing crude commercial salt.
Combines large-scale sedimentation, decantation, and sand/gravel filtration to supply clean drinking water.
Stepwells collect monsoon runoff, minimize evaporation losses, and recharge groundwater aquifers.
applications.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

applications.application_title: Atmospheric Water Generators (AWG) in Arid Zones
applications.description: Condenses humidity directly from ambient air to supply potable drinking water in drought regions.
applications.source_reference: Chapter 8: A Journey through States of Water

applications.application_title: Soil Conservation via Afforestation and Tree Root Anchorage
applications.description: Planting trees on hillslopes binds topsoil with root networks, preventing rainwater erosion and landslides.
